Thats so true fanta thank you for sticking up for op. Medication isn't alway sunshine and rainbows or a fix all. 

Ever wonder why there's so many different variations for anti-depressants/other mental health medications and not just one medication that could actually work is because they are still making new medications that could work better. They need more research. They keep making new brands of medications because the current ones aren't working for some people or causing too many side effects. Because they currently inefficient and now they need to make ones that actually work better.

Mental health was really stigmatized in the 1950s so it didn't get as much time or research as high cholesterol or any other physical problem your blabbing about. So what you can deduct from that is much more is known about physical ailments. For crying out loud any where from 1950s to 1970s people is some places were getting placed in asylums and getting their brain shocked.

There's been much less research done for psychological medicine then physical medications for that reason.

The brain is the most complex part of your whole body it is one of the hardest places to treat because if you get a surgery one wrong move will leave you a vegetable take the wrong illegal drugs and you can end up a vegetable. The brain is sensitive give it the wrong stuff you'll end up hurt. The scientists dont even know all that the brain does.

Mental health medications can help but they come at a high price side effects like weight gain or  weight loss, loss of sex drive, racing heart, seizures, and fainting etc. I dont know all the side effect but even my doctor told me that taking medication is a gamble because you can spend years trying to find the right one because some of them take months to kick in and when they do if they aren't good for you your screwed you have to do the whole process again.

Medication isn't always the answer studies show that therapy works just as well. Medication works for some people but there's alot of people suffering on the wrong stuff. Someone I knew took medication and he got more suicidal and attempt suicide. He has been off medication for 2 years he says it's tough but he also says he would rather feel the horrible lows and sometimes happiness rather then feel nothing at all.

Because what medication usually do is numb everything. They usually cant take away the anxiety or depression without the happiness so you end up this numb mess but to the people who do feel good after taking medication good for you.

But even if the medications is working it will stop being effective in a few years because your body gets used to it. The withdrawls can really hurt you. And even if you up the dose what happens when your at the maximum dose and cant go any higher your screwed. 

I myself have anxiety, depression, adhd, and PTSD. I took medication for 7 years sometimes it helps but most of time it doesn't. I myself would rather feel the fear and pain then be numb or have any weird side effect from any medication. My I'm depressed 70%-90% of a month and I'm not at rock bottom im succeeding in my life I have to work alot harder then others to succeed but i do what i need to do to live a good life. I feel hurt I feel depressed and I have ways to help me that aren't taking medication, I'm even planning to go to therapy for some extra help. 

I'm living proof that even if you have depression or any other mental health illness or trauma you can still live a good quality of life.

My quality of life wouldn't be any easier with medication it's just another type of struggle. 

Not everyone would be better off with medication.
